reviewerOrPass: Worker A, same AI, separate source-first pass
method: After freezing the record, started again from the 2026–2027 regulations, the current study guide and the current course workbook. Reconstructed year totals, checked route neutrality and the competency exam chain, then reconsidered every schedule and positive alignment before comparing with the canonical.
findings: The 2026–2027 regulations identify the full-time 180 EC Medicine bachelor (ISAT 56551). Articles 4.1 and 7.1 set annual totals of 60 EC. Shared Causes of Diseases modules and cumulative Knowledge Development sit alongside longitudinal Competency Development. Sustainable Care is the first-listed of four communities for the same competency slots, with no general route designated. The official ordering resolves the tie independently of UCR. The public programme page describes Dutch instruction for new entrants. Transitional rules for the former English route do not define the current entrant curriculum. No free-choice minor is added.

Article 5.2 normally requires 45 first-year credits for positive binding study advice. Article 6.1 requires meeting that threshold for year two and completing all 60 first-year credits for year three under ordinary progression. Article 9.3 sequences Knowledge Development B1 to B2 to B3, Competency Development 1.1 to 2.1 to 3.1 and 1.2 to 2.2, with both 2.2 and 3.1 required before 3.2. The July study guide pp. 36–38 adds the approved proposal requirement. Research is undertaken in teams of three to five with individual work and assessment in the 20 EC final competency block. The UCR optional element is a separately displayed 15 EC opportunity and outside all 180 EC schedules.

The guide describes infection and immune function in 1.3, neoplasms in 1.2, heart and lung disease in 2.2, neurological symptoms and cognition in 3.2 and psychiatric disorders in 3.3. Matching workbook rows document host defence, cellular injury and neoplasia, organ system disease, consciousness and cognition, and specific psychiatric disorders. Other placements, progress tests and consultation blocks have no sufficient course-level equivalence. Independent UCR research is optional and excluded from the course schedule.

Biomedical science progresses from cell biology, anatomy, physiology and biochemistry to immune mechanisms, organ pathology, pharmacology, molecular genetics and laboratory work. Probability, numerical methods and research synthesis develop transferable analytical skills without implying medical practice. Health psychology progresses from brain and social psychology to health behaviour, psychological assessment and communication, with qualitative methods and research synthesis. Leadership and AI ethics support context, and do not establish patient consultation, interprofessional competencies or healthcare innovation training. Description-only Behavioral Economics contributes decision bias, heuristics and experiments. Population health progresses from epidemiology and sociology to prevention, inequalities, ageing, public economics and description-supported econometrics in causal and predictive analysis. Description-only Environmental Justice adds comparative case work and social movement theory; it supplies environmental and equity context, not medical exposure assessment. Each retained option differs in research questions and course spine. The case has only three coherent target-related concepts at this breadth. Community labels describe Groningen’s training contexts and do not warrant additional UCR programmes built around clinical practice. Removed weak alignments to clinical competency and retained five specifically supported biomedical or psychological alignments. Groningen’s patient care, exams, supervised practice and competency programme remain separate.
